html:
SMTO-GWT-0075 — The GPU action was stopped before it finished

GUID: cd3c70aa-08bf-599b-9190-9b503f92c102
Slug: gpu-operation-cancelled
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • A stop request reached this GPU action before it was done. If it was a settings change, the change may or may not have taken effect.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to show the current details for this GPU, without asking for any change. For power, persistence or compute mode changes, the details show whether the new value is already in place.
  2. Only if the details still show the old value, ask SMTO for the change again. Asking again after the change already took effect could change a card that programs are now using.
  3. If you had asked to change clock speeds or reset the GPU, don't ask again; send the details to the person who manages that computer. SMTO can't tell from a reading whether a clock lock or reset took effect, so repeating it could cause harm.

What success looks like

  • The GPU details show the setting you wanted, or you repeated the change once after confirming it hadn't happened.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't repeat a GPU reset or clock change to find out whether the first one worked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GPU operation checkpoint observed the cancellation event before completion; a configuration whose nvidia-smi command was still running is reported as gpu.operation_outcome_unknown instead, but a narrow race means a configuration may still have completed, so its effect is not guaranteed absent.

What this means

  • A GPU checkpoint observed the cancellation event before completion. Mutation paths separately preserve or reconcile unknown effects if the provider had already started. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A GPU checkpoint observed the cancellation event before completion. Mutation paths separately preserve or reconcile unknown effects if the provider had already started.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect retained samples or mutation receipts and whether provider execution began before cancellation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the receipt (executed, effect_unknown) and the Gateway job named gpu_ plus the execution ID, then read gpu.device for the exact UUID before issuing any new configuration. Never replay a reset or clock change to infer its result.
  • Inspect any retained result before deciding whether another operation is needed.

Retry and execution caution

  • For a mutation, inspect the exact UUID and resolve any active execution or uncertain effect before issuing a new operation. Never replay a reset or an unobservable clock change to infer its result.

How to verify the fix

  • Cancellation is settled and any attempted device change is reconciled for its exact UUID.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
